summary: Server-Sent Events: consumes a streaming HTTP endpoint, with connection state, retries and errors as graph outputs.
description: Opens a `text/event-stream` connection and turns each event into outputs plus an `onMessage` signal. Two transports: Fetch (the default under 'Auto') can send headers, a method and a body, receives every event type, resumes with an explicit `Last-Event-ID`, and can tell a finished stream from a dropped one; EventSource is the browser's own client, which cannot set headers or POST, needs named event types declared up front on `eventTypes`, and reconnects on its own schedule. Failures never disappear: `connectionState` moves through idle/connecting/open/reconnecting/closed/error, `retryCount` counts consecutive failures, `lastError` carries the message and `onError` fires. Retries use exponential backoff from `reconnectDelay` up to `maxReconnectDelay`, honouring a server `retry:` field when one arrives. A 4xx is terminal (retrying cannot help); 5xx, 408 and 429 are retried. Deleting the node or navigating away aborts the request and clears every timer.
whenToUse: Any server-push stream: AI/agent responses streamed token by token, progress on a long-running job, live notifications, dashboard metrics. Use the Fetch transport whenever the endpoint needs an Authorization header or a request body — the usual shape for an AI backend. Use REST2 or HTTP Request for ordinary request/response, and a WebSocket node when the client must also send on the same connection. Client-only: the node stays inert during server-side rendering and connects after hydration.

ports.url: Stream endpoint. Required before Connect does anything; an empty URL reports an error rather than failing silently.
ports.transport: 'Auto' picks Fetch wherever fetch exists. Choose 'EventSource' only to get the browser's own reconnection behaviour.
ports.method: Fetch transport only. POST is the common case for an AI endpoint that takes a prompt.
ports.headers: Fetch transport only — an object of header name to value. EventSource cannot send headers at all.
ports.body: Fetch transport only. An object is JSON-encoded and Content-Type is set unless Headers already sets it.
ports.eventTypes: Comma-separated named event types. Only needed for EventSource, which delivers a named event only to a listener registered in advance.
ports.textPath: Where the text lives inside a JSON payload, as a dot path — `choices.0.delta.content` for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint. Blank for a stream that sends bare text. Whatever it names appears on `text`.
ports.autoConnect: Connects once the URL and the rest of the inputs have landed, without needing a Connect signal.
ports.autoReconnect: Retry after a failure. Off means a single failure goes straight to the error state.
ports.reconnectOnStreamEnd: Off by default. An agent response stream is finite, and reconnecting would re-issue the request and start the response again.
ports.maxRetries: 0 keeps retrying. Otherwise the connection reports an error naming the budget it spent.
ports.dedupeById: Drops events whose id was already seen, so a resumed reconnect cannot re-deliver messages. Turn off only if the server reuses ids for distinct events.
ports.connectionState: idle, connecting, open, reconnecting, closed or error. 'error' is terminal; 'reconnecting' means another attempt is coming.
ports.connected: True only while the stream is open — false during connect, backoff and after a terminal failure.
ports.data: The event payload, parsed as JSON when it parses and left as the raw string when it does not (so a `[DONE]` sentinel arrives intact). An *object* for a JSON payload — feed a Text node or a Text Accumulator from `text`, not from here.
ports.raw: The payload exactly as sent, before any JSON parsing.
ports.text: The one data output that is always a string: the payload as sent when `textPath` is blank, or the field at that path when it is set. A missing field, a non-JSON sentinel or a path landing on an object all read as empty rather than as `[object Object]`.
ports.eventType: The `event:` field of the last event, or 'message' when the server sent none.
ports.lastEventId: The furthest `id:` the server has sent; this is what a reconnect resumes from.
ports.deliverySemantics: 'at-most-once' when the server sends no ids (gap events are lost), 'at-least-once' when it does, 'at-least-once-deduped' when ids are present and Dedupe By Id is on.
ports.duplicatesSuppressed: How many replayed events were dropped after a resume. Non-zero is normal after a reconnect.
ports.onMessage: Fires once per event, after the Data outputs have updated — so an accumulator wired `text` → `chunk` and `onMessage` → `add` sees the chunk first.
ports.onClose: Fires when the stream stops, whether cleanly or with a terminal error, so a Close handler always runs.
ports.onError: Fires on every failure, including ones the node is about to retry.

patterns: SSE `text` → Text Accumulator `chunk` and SSE `onMessage` → Text Accumulator `add`, with an empty delimiter, renders an AI response as it is written. Set `textPath` to `choices.0.delta.content` for an OpenAI-compatible endpoint and leave it blank for a stream of bare tokens; either way `text` is a string.
`data` is for the payloads that are meant to be objects: a JSON Stream Parser, or an Action Dispatcher's `action` input.
SSE `connectionState` → String Mapper → a status label makes reconnection visible instead of leaving the UI apparently frozen.
POST the prompt in `body` with an Authorization header rather than putting a token in the query string, which the EventSource-only approach forces.
antiPatterns: Turning on Reconnect On Stream End for a finite agent response — the request is re-issued and the answer regenerates in a loop.
Ignoring `connectionState` and wiring only the data outputs: a silently failing reconnection then looks identical to a slow server.

Wiring `data` into anything that expects text. `data` is JSON-parsed, so for the commonest agent shape (`data: {"delta":"Hi"}`) it is an object; a Text Accumulator refuses it and reports the mis-wiring rather than appending `[object Object]`. Use `text`.
Leaving `textPath` blank on a JSON-envelope stream and wiring `raw` instead — the answer then reads as a run of JSON fragments.
Using the EventSource transport when the endpoint needs an Authorization header, then smuggling the token through the URL.
